1.explanation: 1) In Dropdown.js the `render` method constructs the `<label>` (title) and helper text with `--disabled` classes when the `disabled` prop is true, which lowers their contrast below WCAG AA thresholds. To fix the color contrast violation, the logic that applies `bx--label--disabled` and `bx--form__helper-text--disabled` may need adjustment or removal for the Dropdown variant. 2) In ListBoxField.js the `ListBoxField` component always sets an `aria-label` of “Open menu” or “Close menu” based solely on expansion state, ignoring the visible label text. This causes the accessible name not to match the visible label (“Dropdown menu options”). The ARIA labeling needs to be updated so that the button either uses `aria-labelledby` pointing to the `<label>` or computes an `aria-label` that includes the visible label text.
1.bug_scenario: When the Dropdown is disabled, the label and helper text get the “--disabled” style modifiers and their color drops to a 1.71 contrast ratio, violating WCAG AA. In addition, the dropdown button’s accessible name is hard-coded to “Open menu”/“Close menu” (via aria-label) which does not match or contain the visible selected label text (“Dropdown menu options”), triggering an accessible name mismatch.

2.explanation: The Dropdown.render method in Dropdown.js is responsible for outputting both the visible <label> and the <ListBox.Field> button that users interact with. It currently renders the title text without an id and does not wire up the aria-labelledby attribute on the ListBox.Field, causing the accessible name mismatch. Additionally, it applies low-contrast disabled styles to the label/helper text via titleClasses and helperClasses. The ListBoxField functional component in ListBoxField.js also explicitly sets aria-label to ’Open menu’ or ’Close menu’, overriding any aria-labelledby reference to the visible label text. To fix the name-matching violation, Dropdown.render must assign a stable id to the <label> (e.g. id=`${id}-label`) and pass aria-labelledby to ListBox.Field. To fix contrast violations, the CSS classes for disabled labels/helper text need darker color tokens or alternative styling in both Dropdown and ListBoxField (via titleClasses/helperClasses and defaultTranslations). These two components and their render logic are thus the key bug locations to update.
2.bug_scenario: When rendering a <Dropdown> in React, DAP reports two types of accessibility violations: (1) insufficient color contrast on the disabled label/helper text (contrast of 1.71 against background fails WCAG AA), and (2) “Accessible name must match or contain the visible label text” on the toggle button: the aria-label output by ListBoxField (‘Open menu’/‘Close menu’) doesn’t include or refer to the visible dropdown title (‘Dropdown menu options’).
